text: The following question stood in the name of Assoc Prof Walter Theseira – 1 To ask the Minister for Manpower (a) what steps have been taken to ensure that work pass holders are aware of the COVID-19 control measures and are empowered to report violations of such measures, particularly if violations are encouraged by errant employers; and (b) what has been done to ensure that work pass holders who face cancellation of their work passes due to violating Leave of Absence, Quarantine or other COVID-19 control measures have not done so under duress or misinformation from their employers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Many are available in the work pass holders’ native language and are available on MOM’s website.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Employers have been encouraged to use these materials to do regular briefings to their workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MOM has also asked employers to contact the work pass holders affected by the Leave of Absence or Stay-Home Notice requirements and directly inform them of the measures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Dormitory operators have been displaying many of our posters in their premises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In addition, MOM has been sharing bite-size COVID-19 information to the foreign workers through our foreign worker ambassadors on a daily basis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Videos in various native languages have also been produced to explain the situation and control measures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Ground engagement with foreign workers has been further stepped up with the help of MWC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Employers have to send the MOM approval letter with the Leave of Absence or Stay-Home Notice requirements to their work pass holders before they commence their return.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Work pass holders are aware they face cancellation of their work passes if they violate the COVID-19 control measures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Employers and employees have a joint duty to ensure that the employee behaves responsibly during the Leave of Absence or Stay-Home Notice.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In cases where the work pass holders were asked to work during their Leave of Absence or Stay-Home Notice, they should not comply and instead report their employer to the Ministry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MOM will investigate and take actions against the employer.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: It was mentioned in The Straits Times on 13 February that three workers were issued warning letters when their employers had asked them to go to work.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Will their subsequent employment after their current employment ends, be affected?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Workers who are issued warning letters are usually unable to find subsequent employment when current employment ends.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: The second supplementary question, in a recent Straits Times report – I think it was two days ago – we are also concerned about an additional three workers whose Work Permits were revoked because they did not answer their calls by the Ministry, as the Minister of State alluded to earlier.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: This seems rather harsh and we are wondering if investigations are being conducted to find out why they did not answer their calls.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For the first question, the Member would have noticed, yesterday as well, we announced that we are going to work on change of employment directives for manufacturing as well as services.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These are two areas where today, they are not allowed to do change of employment so easily.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we are facilitating it through the trade associations, companies and industry representatives.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If Members know of such workers, please do refer them to us and we will have organisations or partners, such as MWC, to see how we can support them.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On the second point, it is also important for us to signal that for a public health measure, we cannot take this too lightly.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: When workers fail to respond, I am sure they have valid reasons.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We go down and investigate each one of them.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: There are a variety of reasons why they cannot respond, the most common is, "My phone cannot get a signal" and so forth.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The reality is you have the whole day to respond.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: When they cannot account for where they were, then it becomes a bit more difficult to explain.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In the interest of public health, you have to take a check.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is where we have to take action.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And I have to thank employers as well as workers for cooperating with us on all our measures, whether it is Leave of Absence, Stay-Home Notice or the quarantine measures, to ensure that public health is maintained, public safety is maintained.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And we manage the situation as best as we can.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: For local or foreign workers, in light of the required five-day medical certificates (MCs) that are issued by doctors for flu or fever during this COVID-19 period, whether MOM can classify these MCs given out as COVID-19 MCs and outside of the scope or ambit of the 14 days of Sick Leave under the Employment Act.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Otherwise, the suggestion would be to classify it instead as Hospitalisation Leave under the Employment Act so that a worker will not over consume the 14-day Sick Leave entitlement under the Employment Act.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I said Leave of Absence and Stay-Home Notice earlier, but I think even MCs today are an important part of the health measures that we have to undertake.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Employers can treat the five-day MCs as part of the employees' outpatient Sick Leave entitlement, or alternatively, as the Member suggested, if they wish to provide more support to the employees, employers can also treat the five-day MC as part of the employees' Hospitalisation Leave entitlement.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If an employee were to have insufficient outpatient Sick Leave in the future, employers are encouraged to be flexible and compassionate, and grant additional Sick Leave to the employee to take into consideration the prolonged Sick Leave used for the COVID-19 situation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But generally, for MCs of five days, you will not exceed either one.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We are publishing a list of Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) to provide clearer guidance to employers on the issue.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we are hoping to get the link ready, either by today or tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand the rationale of making sure that our workers come back only with approval.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But it is the employer who submits the application to MOM for approval.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Again, the measures are in place because public health is at stake.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, in this case, I think we have to also take a really bird's eye view on how we want to deal with the issue, and in which everyone – both the employer and worker – has to cooperate.
